gaps.wanted: The 48Y's weight. Table 31 gives 30.00 lb (13.60 kg); the installation safety text gives 20.78 to 21.16 lb (9.43 to 9.6 kg) with the power supplies and fans installed. Same measure and scope as far as either says, so it is a conflict; Table 31's figure is used.

What the lamp under the unlabelled sixth position (port 5's down arrow) is. The photograph prints PS0, PS1, Diag, Fan and Loc under five lamps and nothing under the sixth; it is drawn as port 5's lamp.
Which port each of the four lamps in a QSFP28 column band, and the two lamps in each lower cage, belongs to. The guide says four blue and amber lamps a port and that only the first is used.
The coloured boxes and brackets of the lane legends under SFP28 ports 16 to 39 and the 50 and 53 boxes under ports 46 and 47; only their numerals are drawn, and the guide does not say what they mean.
The USB revision. The guide names one USB port and gives no generation.
The depth of the fan module and of the power supplies. The guide's figures are isometric and carry no scale and its tables state weights only.

a `power-draw-max-w` on each module this chassis accepts, from the vendor's own per-card table - Cisco publishes one per ambient, most vendors publish none, and until they land a module total is a floor
`physical-context` on 8 bays (rear 8); `physical-context` on port groups qsfp28, sfp28 - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

chassis.note: guide Table 31: 1.71 in (4.34 cm) high, 17.25 in (43.81 cm) wide, 20.27 in (51.48 cm) deep, 30.00 lb (13.60 kg). The inch figures are converted (43.43, 438.15 and 514.86 mm). The width is the body between the ear folds; the guide says the outer edges of the brackets make 19 in, so the brackets are not modelled. THE WEIGHT CONFLICTS with the installation safety text, which says the 48Y weighs 20.78 to 21.16 lb (9.43 to 9.6 kg) with the power supplies and fans installed; Table 31 is used and the conflict is a gap. The 32C's two sources agree at 23.5 lb.

chassis-lamps.note: Table 16: PS1 and PS2 (green working, amber faulty, unlit absent), Diag (always green), FAN (green normal, amber faulty, unlit powered off) and LOC (amber flashing on a remote command). The photograph prints them as PS0 and PS1, Diag, Fan and Loc, so those legends are drawn.

colour.note: The front plate samples #696769 on the top-left corner and #6d6c6f at the right end; the chassis colour is #6b6d71. The rear panel samples #666465. The photographs are lit warmly and these are their values, not a paint reference.

ears-and-kits.note: The guide mounts the 48Y flush with the front of a four-post 19 in rack with the standard brackets (recessed mounting is named for the 32C only). One flush position is written, with no kit. The rack mount kit is NOT MODELLED and is not in `chassis.kits`: QFX520048Y-RMKT (front mounting brackets, rear mounting brackets, flat-head M4 x 6 mm and washer-head screws), also the spare's order number. Rack rail spacing 23.5 to 30.6 in.

gate-1.note: Figure 16 (a 3000 x 868 px raster of the port side) is orthographic enough to measure: its outline measures 2853 px between stroke centres (x 23.5 to 2876.5) and 282 px (y 288.5 to 570.5), an aspect of 10.12 against the table's 438.15 / 43.43 = 10.09, at 6.51 px/mm. The studio photograph agrees (body 62 to 2018 px, 4.467 px/mm, 43 mm high). The rear figure 26 (1501 x 319 px) reads 1426.5 x 142 px, 10.05, at 3.256 px/mm, and the rear photograph 1948 x 192 px, 10.1, at 4.446 px/mm.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life announcement. No Juniper notice was found and the guide states none, so the device states none announced. Estimated, because no maker page was searched beyond the guide.

mgmt-panel.note: At the right, in a silver housing: the RJ45 management port above (Mgmt) and the RJ45 console below (Console), with the legend "Mgmt up-arrow, down-arrow Console" and "RUNNING JUNOS" under them; the guide's callouts 3 and 4 do not say which is which and the photograph's legend settles it. They are 12.7 mm cells, 14.0 apart, mirrored (the upper has its contacts at the foot). The USB port is under the SFP28 block at 326.9 mm (figure 16, callout 6) and the reset pinhole at 51.7 mm with its legend (callout 7 is the lamp row).

modules.note: The fan modules (QFX520048Y-FAN-AO and -AI) and the power supplies (QFX520048Y-APSU-AO and -AI) are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component of this family. The 48Y's supplies are NOT the JPSU-650W-AC-AO and -AI of the QFX5120: different part number, one lamp and not three, a different face (guide figures 35 and 38 against the QFX5120's). Nothing on this chassis is a built-in unit that is not a bay.

port-lamps.note: One lamp a SFP28 port, an up arrow for the even port and a down arrow for the odd one, between the rows (figure 18, Table 10: amber steady for link, amber blinking for activity). THE FIRST THREE COLUMNS ARE DIFFERENT: the photograph prints PS0, PS1, Diag, Fan and Loc under their lamps, and guide Table 16 lists five chassis status LEDs on the port side, so those five are drawn as the chassis lamps and the sixth (under port 5) as port 5's lamp, which the guide does not name. Each QSFP28 column has a band of four lamps (arrow, two rings, arrow); the guide says only that the QSFP28 ports have four blue and amber lamps, that only the first is used, and that the arrow lamps of 48, 49, 51 and 52 are not used. The mapping of the rings to ports and the two lamps in each lower cage are READ OFF THE PHOTOGRAPH AND ESTIMATED.

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal and read off the photograph and figure 16: the SFP28 ports run 0 to 47, even above odd, as "0 up-arrow, down-arrow 1" legends under each column (the arrows point at the lamps between the rows); the QSFP28 ports print 48 and 49, 51 and 52 under the stacked pairs and 50 and 53 in lane-legend boxes at the lower right. Interface names are not printed and are not written. The 12 port groups of four SFP28 ports (Table 8) are not printed.

ports.note: Figure 16, 48 SFP28 cages in two rows of 24 columns, in three gangs of eight columns on the registry's 14.25 mm pitch (a gang measures 742 px, 114.0 mm), 3.1 mm apart; the first gang starts 14.7 mm from the left and the QSFP28 block 365.2 mm. The rows are 14.6 mm apart (cells from 2.6 and 17.2 mm down); the photograph's cage openings are about 8 mm high with a metal lamp tray 8.6 mm tall between them, narrower than the registry's 10.4 mm cell, so THE CELLS ARE THE REGISTRY'S AND THE OPENINGS ARE ESTIMATED. The six QSFP28 cages are two columns on the registry's 19.0 pitch in THREE rows: a stacked pair with a lamp band between them (centres 7.5 and 23.6 mm down, ports 48 and 49 on the left, 51 and 52 on the right) and a single cage below each (36.5 mm, ports 50 and 53), which figure 16 shows as callouts 2 (four cages) and 5 (two cages).

power.note: Table 20 (AC): 382 W typical and 430 W maximum, input 100 to 240 VAC at 7.8 A (100 to 120 V) or 3.8 A (200 to 240 V). Table 25 (DC): 315 W typical and 470 W maximum, -48 to -60 VDC rated, 21 A. The AC pair is filed as the device's, since AC is the default build.

rear-layout.note: Rear photograph at 4.446 px/mm and figure 26 at 3.256 px/mm: a power supply at each end (frame 50.4 mm wide, its red latch overhanging the frame by 3.9 mm on the left), six fan modules between them on a 48.6 mm pitch (face 39.9 mm wide from 77.6 mm, with an 8.3 mm flange carrying the captive screw to its left), and a ground screw at each end of the panel. The photograph and the figure agree to 1 mm everywhere both can be measured except the latch (the photograph magnifies the proud latch). The panel carries no connectors and no lamps: the 48Y has no fan lamps (guide) and its power supplies carry their own.

rear-photo-vs-drawing.note: The photograph shows front-to-back (AIR OUT) fan modules with red handles lettered F2B. Table 17 gives the label as AIR OUT; the photograph wins for that module. The guide's flat figure 26 draws the modules without labels.

sources.note: Juniper QFX5200 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2026-03-09, 236 pages (copyright 2026 Juniper Networks): the port panel figures 13, 16, 17, 18 and 21, the management and status figures 22 and 24, the FRU panel figure 26, the fan and power supply figures 28, 35, 38 and 40 to 44, the specification tables 3, 8 to 10, 13, 14, 16, 17, 19, 20, 24, 25, 30 and 31 and the mounting chapter. Juniper's studio photographs of the 48Y, front and rear, 2100 x 464 and 2100 x 424 px (image library, qfx5200-48y-front-high and -rear-high). THE HPE DATASHEET (a00150814enw) DID NOT ANSWER, a transport error on the one attempt, so no datasheet figure is used. No mechanical drawing and no 3D model were found. The held intake folders (SOURCES.md, COVERAGE.md) are on another machine and could not be read from this one, so no held photograph, stencil or model was available to use.

stack-orientation.note: The library's stack convention: an upper cage upright over a lower one turned 180, so both lips face the band between the rows. The photograph's cages are too dark to confirm it at the SFP28 rows, so the rule decides and a photograph overturns it. The single QSFP28 cages in the third row are upright.

vents.note: Hexagonal perforations: a column at the left end (3 to 36 mm down), a band along the foot (37.6 to 42.6 mm, interrupted by the USB port and the QSFP28 cages) and a column at the right end. A dark label plate runs under the SFP28 block. Positions are read at 4.467 px/mm and are estimated.
